h2: Pipeline inspection in North Texas: who regulates the line and what NDE the dig needs
html:
Pipeline inspection in North Texas: who regulates the line and what NDE the dig needs

Pipeline inspection around Dallas usually means NDE at integrity digs, on station piping and on new or replaced sections, carried out for an operator whose line falls under the Railroad Commission of Texas or PHMSA. Atlantis sends crews from Houston for ultrasonic, magnetic particle, radiographic, visual and holiday testing, while the operator's integrity engineers keep the assessment and repair decisions.

Who regulates the line. The Railroad Commission's Pipeline Safety Department regulates intrastate pipelines in Texas, covering gas distribution, gas transmission and hazardous liquid lines, including highly volatile liquids and any line that crosses a navigable waterway. Only some gathering lines are covered: gas gathering is classified under 49 CFR 192.8 and 192.9, and hazardous liquid gathering is regulated in non-rural areas or where it meets the rural criteria in 49 CFR 195.11. On top of Parts 192 and 195, the Commission applies its own rules in 16 TAC Chapter 8 and damage-prevention rules in Chapter 18. Interstate pipelines are PHMSA's. Settle this before the dig, because it decides whose procedures, report format and record retention the NDE must follow.

The local system. The Barnett Shale natural gas field lies beneath Fort Worth, and by 2011 Railroad Commission figures showed about 2,700 wells in Tarrant County alone, none of which can produce without a gathering line. Because so much of that pipe runs through built-up neighborhoods, class location, and so the level of regulation, matters more here than in open country. Dallas is also headquarters to Energy Transfer, a midstream operator, and to Atmos Energy, a gas distribution utility, so integrity, replacement and compliance programs for large systems are planned from the Metroplex.

NDE that a North Texas integrity dig typically calls for:

  • A UT thickness grid or corrosion map over the reported metal-loss feature, recorded so it can be matched to the in-line inspection call
  • Magnetic particle or ACFM examination of dents, gouges and the long seam for cracking
  • Pit-depth and external corrosion measurements with photographs of coating condition
  • Holiday testing of new coating before backfill
  • Radiography or automated UT of girth welds on replacement pipe to API 1104

What makes dig data usable. A dig report is only useful when it can be lined up with the in-line inspection feature list, the girth weld numbering and the operator's integrity management records. Atlantis reports give location references, technician certification, instrument calibration and the procedure revision used, and the Atlantis ERP keeps those records linked so a regulator's request can be answered years later.

The individual services are described on the holiday testing, ACFM inspection and automated UT pages. New stations and line sections are covered under commissioning inspection, and the full menu is at NDT inspection services. Operators who need a pipeline NDE procedure written or reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III can use procedure development. To plan digs or a station campaign, send the feature list, locations and target dates through the North Texas pipeline request.
